context_boundaries.shared_entrypoints_are_indexes: AGENTS.md is the canonical repository index and CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md are one-line @AGENTS.md imports. Shared entrypoints may contain identity, mandatory index paths, context routing, session-contract locations, and permanent safety boundaries only; never current goals, issue state, implementation plans, completion claims, or artifact wording.
context_boundaries.recovery_mode: A .codex/no-harness, .claude/no-harness, or .pi/no-harness marker at the resolved project root or any ancestor is an explicit local recovery escape hatch: the marker is inherited by descendant checkouts, repository session-contract mutation checks are bypassed for that checkout, and no contract is created or bound. This marker does not claim to change host or operating-system permissions. A marker-free checkout uses the gate's normal policy path.
context_boundaries.session_contract_authority: Outside recovery mode, an UNBOUND session may perform ordinary reversible file creation and editing inside its resolved project boundary, plus policy-approved routine local shell work such as inspection, tests, builds, and non-destructive Git operations. A BOUND contract is required for governance or host-policy files, shared entrypoints, deletion, destructive or remote operations, external effects, and any operation that can expand the session's own authority. Once bound, every non-read-only shell command must exactly match a digest-covered allowed_shell_commands entry; routine status does not exempt it. When bound, the local registry pointer, active contract digest, explicit session_bindings entry, and progress contract reference must all agree. Progress or Markdown session_id fields never grant authority.
context_boundaries.project_isolation: Never infer a session binding from a parent workspace, child project, or the repository's only unfinished work unit. Concurrent contracts must declare non-overlapping target_ownership paths.
context_boundaries.context_is_not_output: Background, reference, example, conversation, and internal context constrain reasoning but are not code, UI, or external-document content. Rendering requires explicit atom-level derive, quote, or require authority for a declared output unit and audience.
context_boundaries.source_atom_contract: Every v2 source atom declares subject, effect, and render_policy. Non-directive source classifications keep directive_ids exactly empty; rendering authority never becomes objective authority.
context_boundaries.output_unit_contract: Every verifiable v2 output unit declares kind, audience, exposure, objective_atom_ids, and content_source_atom_ids. Agent-workflow background/precondition atoms cannot be shipping content edges.

ai_workflow.lightweight_workflow: development-cycle.yaml (non-feature changes: typos, config values, simple directives)
mandatory_pre_checks: When working in submodule, read its entry point file

For feature-level work: follow issue-driven-development.yaml material-decision checkpoints (understand → scope → plan); an explicit bounded request proceeds without repeated confirmation, while an unresolved choice that materially changes the result must be asked
For any .hwp/.hwpx/.pdf/.docx/.xlsx/.pptx file: use /read-doc skill FIRST — never claim inability to read documents

Design docs (docs/design/, spec/, design/) + extensions (.md/.txt/.yaml/.json): see ai_workflow.permission_model in .agents/context/agents-rules-detail.json. Hook fires on edits — surface reason to user first.
Before running destructive git commands (git checkout --, git reset --hard, git clean -f): ALWAYS ask user for explicit confirmation first. State exactly what will be deleted. No exceptions.

Before a material, irreversible, ambiguous, or out-of-scope deletion: understand the exact target and impact, preserve a recovery path where practical, and get user confirmation. Agent-owned temporary/work artifact cleanup and a user-requested bounded recoverable deletion may proceed without repeated approval after exact-target verification. (see dead_code_safety)
ai_workflow.submodule_rule: Each submodule has own rules. Read entry_point before modifications.

language_harness.no_korean_in_agents: Use concise English for machine-facing .agents/ files by default. Korean is allowed when a user explicitly requests it, when preserving a Korean user-facing trigger/example is necessary, or when localized human-facing text is part of the contract; machine JSON/YAML keys remain stable.
language_harness.concise_session_output: AI responses should be extremely brief (less than 3 lines) to minimize history weight. Avoid long Korean preambles.

conventions.test_code_review: After writing tests, never trust results blindly. Review test logic itself with iterative review (2 consecutive clean passes) before trusting outcomes. Signs of invalid tests: assertions that always pass, mocked internals that diverge from real behavior, missing negative cases.

workflows.instruction: Read workflows on demand. Do not load all at once.

steps: Extract keywords from the user request
Read the matching root quick reference first
Load the workflow document only if the task still needs details

public_repository_release_gate.policy: FAIL CLOSED: Before creating a public repository, changing a repository to public, publishing or updating a public template, or pushing content copied from a private workspace into a public repository, complete and record a public-safety review. A private destination does not make source material safe when its template or upstream is public.

token_budget_policy.on_demand_loading: Beyond the mandatory session-start reads, load only the project-index.yaml on_demand_loading section needed for the task; never bulk-load a full body context file (matches A.4: separate entrypoint vs body files to prevent index bloat).
token_budget_policy.reserve_for_compact: Reserve compact output space before the window is full — never wait for overflow then handle it as an emergency.
token_budget_policy.restore_after_compact: After compact, reconstruct work semantics: active plan, loaded skills, key files, tool state (post-compact-context.js hook).
token_budget_policy.layered_lifetimes: Keep long-lived rules, persistent memory, session continuity, and temporary dialogue as distinct layers with different entry costs.
token_budget_policy.resend_cost: Every model call resends the system prompt, tool definitions, entrypoints, every file read, and the whole conversation; session length and always-loaded text set usage. Measurements: docs/archive/2026-09-23-context-budget-measurements.md.
token_budget_policy.always_loaded_size: Keep entrypoints and mandatory reads within .agents/context/context-budget.json; procedures, incident lessons, and history go to docs/.
token_budget_policy.large_reads: Read files over about 20KB by range or search, diffs with --stat first, and logs or JSON in slices.
token_budget_policy.delegate_exploration: A root session coordinates; broad searches, reviews, and multi-file edits run in subagents or one-shot headless calls that return a summary.
token_budget_policy.session_rollover: Past about 200K tokens of context, write a handoff and continue in a fresh session. Each tool's auto-compact limit is set in its own configuration as a backstop; see docs/archive/2026-09-23-context-budget-measurements.md.

detail.rule: Rules below are one line each. The detail file keeps the full text under the same key paths; read only the section a task touches. Code reads the merge of both files.

sections.ai_workflow.ask_user_question_format: Decision questions: re-ground in 1-2 sentences, ask without jargon, give an explicit recommendation with completeness score (1-10) and AI and review time, then lettered options each with effort, completeness, and a one-sentence trade-off.
sections.ai_workflow.completeness_principle: Build approved work completely (edge cases, errors, tests). Never add unrequested scope. Keep fork deltas from upstream minimal.
sections.ai_workflow.dead_code_safety: Dead code is not harmless; never casually delete or ignore it. Before material, irreversible, ambiguous, or out-of-scope deletion, understand why it is dead, resolve the exact target and impact, preserve recovery, and get explicit user confirmation. Agent-owned temporary artifacts with an explicit lifecycle and user-requested recoverable deletions proceed without a prompt only after exact-target verification.
sections.ai_workflow.documentation_impact_policy: A production change is complete only when repository docs, user manual, and reusable learning are each recorded as UPDATED (changed files or immutable commit URLs) or N/A (a concrete reason; bare 'not relevant' is invalid) in one per-issue JSON receipt, finalized at Sync and required before Commit.
sections.ai_workflow.escalation_path: A gap between design and implementation goes to the user with options (update design, fix implementation, accept deviation); neither side is silently changed, and the agent waits for the decision.
sections.ai_workflow.permission_model: AI implements code freely. Design docs (docs/design/, design/, spec/ with .md/.txt/.yaml/.json; hook-enforced) are reviewed, not rewritten: autonomous edits are limited to typos, contradictions, and broken links, plus design records the user's current bounded request explicitly asks for (no second approval). Any product, architecture, interface, policy, destructive-disposition, or scope decision not determined by the request goes to the user. Never rewrite design to match implementation.
sections.ai_workflow.requirements_management: Requirements live in .agents/requirements/ and are read on Plan and Review. Candidate REQs yield to code; human REQs bind code. Retrofitted requirements always start as candidate and need explicit human promotion. Trace by file and symbol, never line numbers.
sections.ai_workflow.review_skill: Use /review-pass per stage; feature-level work needs REQ-IDs, lightweight changes (<3 files, one module) do not.
sections.ai_workflow.routine_action_authorization: A bounded task authorizes its normal path (inspection, in-scope edits, local verification, non-force push, delegation) without repeated questions; delegates inherit the objective, scope, and exception boundary. Ask only for: material deletion or any unrecoverable data loss; force push, history rewrite, or forced unrelated-histories merge; unrequested external messages or publication; payments, purchases, paid provisioning, or costly cloud work; production-destructive mutation, production data writes, or irreversible deployment; material scope change or a missing user choice; substituting a different repository, remote, branch lineage, or visibility (a -public/-pub sibling or a search hit is never the named repository; if already done, say so in the reply's first line). This grants no authority over governance files, entrypoints, contracts, credentials, or production.

Unbound sessions may run commands by default; destructive, privileged, remote-transfer, publish, and force or history-rewriting commands, git push, git checkout and git restore, and governance, entrypoint, contract, or registry writes need a session contract. Hidden forms (wrappers, inline -c, command substitution, eval) are resolved and judged, not refused. The command lists are in the detail file; hooks read the merge of both files.
sections.ai_workflow.routine_execution_authority: Never turn workflow checkpoints, tool permissions, session boundaries, or delegation into repeated approval questions; every delegate inherits the same authority. Ask only for irreversible deletion, force push, remote-ref deletion, exceptional forced integration, external messages or publication, payments, production or shared-database mutation, credentials, material cloud cost, or a choice that materially changes the objective.
sections.cascadeRules: Adding or removing a submodule, or changing rules or entrypoints, propagates in order: self, parent, siblings, children, .users mirror. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md stay the one-line @AGENTS.md import, never copies.
sections.context_governance: Provenance notes: runtime context budgeting only, separate from the naia-memory product axis.
sections.conventions.contribution_fork_policy: Contribution forks live under nextain with the upstream name and a README stating purpose, upstream link, status, and contact. AGENTS.md lives on the fork's main only; never add it to a feature branch that goes upstream.
sections.conventions.external_repo_policy: Third-party and community repositories: read their guide, search for duplicates, match the community's tone, draft, and get user approval of the reviewed content before posting anything. AI-assisted external posts always carry a disclosure footer with a contact point (hook-enforced).
sections.conventions.git_workflow: Maintainers direct-push only where repository policy permits; external contributions use pull requests (pr-guard allows only explicit --repo nextain/<repo>). An explicitly requested post in a Nextain or user-owned repository needs no second approval.
sections.conventions.tmp_files: Scratch scripts go under tmp/ of the active working directory; never tmp-* or tmp_* files in repository roots.
sections.conventions.workfile_lifecycle: Work files follow a lifecycle: .agents/context/ is permanent and never deleted; .agents/work/ is temporary but only the user cleans it (no AI auto-delete); tmp/ is scratch; a progress MD/JSON pair moves to .agents/progress/archive/YYYY-MM/ only after the completion criteria hold (AI never self-declares complete), with current_phase closed or unbound first; handoff documents are never staged or committed, and cross-machine handoff goes through a GitHub issue plus commit SHAs, never session files through Git.
sections.financial_integrity: Estimate cost and get explicit user approval before large cloud operations: storage moves over 10GB or over 1,000 API operations through mounts, high-tier GPUs, batch inference or fine-tuning, large database migrations or index rebuilds.
sections.infrastructure: Never write prod gateway credentials to .env.local (.env.local = dev, .env.production.local = prod; hook-enforced). Never attach a self-hosted runner to a public repository. sync-prod-to-dev.sh is manual only and overwrites all dev data. Gateway and runner details are in the detail file.
sections.public_repository_release_gate: Before any public push, visibility change, or public-template publication, review the whole tree and reachable history for secrets, personal data, and private names, record the evidence, and get the repository owner's explicit approval of that exact reviewed commit (any later change voids it). A leak is handled by revoking credentials first; a cleanup commit never closes it. Full scope, evidence, incident response, and the deterministic remote-identity gate are in the detail file.
sections.reference_submodules: Read-only upstream reference repositories (ref-*) used for architecture and pattern research.
sections.skills: Mandatory skills: /read-doc for .hwp/.hwpx/.pdf/.docx/.xlsx/.pptx (never say a file type cannot be read); /webapp-testing for local web UI verification (never ask the user to test manually); /doc-coauthoring before a spec, proposal, RFC, design doc, PRD, or decision record.
